transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I've been losing a lot of weight recently because I'm barely eating. I've just been skipping most of my meals, or only having a tiny bite or two when I do eat.
How do you feel about this weight loss—are you actively trying to lose weight because you feel you need to, or have you just lost your appetite?

I am actively trying to lose weight because I still feel way too big when I look in the mirror. I have an intense fear of gaining anything back, so I have to strictly limit what I eat to make sure that doesn't happen.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel you lose control and eat a large amount of food, or do you ever make yourself throw up or use laxatives to control your weight?
No, I never lose control like that, and I don't throw up or use laxatives. I just focus on strictly limiting how much I eat and avoiding food as much as possible to keep my weight down.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia Nervosa. Based on the patient's report of severe food restriction, significant weight loss, distorted body image, and intense fear of gaining weight, combined with the explicit denial of binge eating, self-induced vomiting, or laxative use, Bulimia Nervosa has been ruled out, leaving Anorexia Nervosa as the definitive diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits severe restriction of energy intake leading to significant weight loss, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted body image (feeling 'way too big' despite weight loss). The absence of binge-eating or purging behaviors supports the restricting subtype of Anorexia Nervosa, while ruling out Bulimia Nervosa and Binge-Eating Disorder.
